body: Rialto Capital Advisors, acting as special servicer for a securitized mortgage loan trust, filed a foreclosure complaint in the Circuit Court of Cook County on Tuesday, March 31, 2026, against New York-based landlord Jenel over the retail building at 36 South State Street in the Chicago Loop, The Real Deal reported, citing court records. The property is just under 19,000 square feet.

Jenel bought the property from Joe Sitt's Thor Equities in 2018 for $26 million, putting in more than $9 million of equity and taking over the existing $16.8 million loan. The complaint alleges the balance was not repaid when the loan matured in June. Rialto now claims a total debt of $17.7 million, including default interest and liquidation fees.

The default came even though the building was performing. Citing loan servicer notes collected by Morningstar Credit, The Real Deal reported that the property was fully leased with a debt service coverage ratio of 1.84 as of September, that revenue reached $1.9 million in the first nine months of 2025, and that net operating income was $1.4 million over that period. Five Below has leased 14,300 square feet there since 2022, after Blick Art Materials moved out. The property's appraised value, however, fell to $13.5 million in July, nearly 48 percent below its value a decade earlier, and the loan moved to special servicing after the maturity default.
Neither Jenel nor Rialto responded to The Real Deal's requests for comment. The publication reported that the Cook County court had set a hearing for Sept. 28.

timeline.label: Jenel buys the property from Thor Equities for $26M, taking over the existing $16.8M loan
Loan matures unpaid, according to the complaint
Rialto Capital Advisors files a $17.7M foreclosure complaint in Cook County
